Field Service Engineer
 
The most valuable field engineers are the ones who can handle the whole job, mechanical and electrical, on their own.
 
This is a Field Service Engineer role for exactly that kind of engineer.
 
As a multi-skilled Field Service Engineer, you will keep high-precision CNC machine tools running for customers across the UK, handling both the mechanical and electrical side of the job yourself. Working for a leading supplier and service provider of advanced CNC machinery, you will travel between sites servicing, installing, diagnosing and repairing lathes and machining centres, whatever the fault turns out to be. No two days look the same, and because you cover both disciplines, you get the full variety of the work and the satisfaction of seeing each job through end to end. If you are an all-rounder who knows CNC machinery and enjoys the independence of life on the road, this role will use everything you have got.
 
Job Responsibilities
  • Travelling to customer sites across the UK, and occasionally Europe, to service, repair and install CNC machine tools
  • Carrying out both mechanical and electrical fault finding and diagnosis on CNC lathes and machining centres
  • Replacing ballscrews, linear guides and spindles, and carrying out gib adjustment and scraping
  • Replacing drives, power supplies and electrical components, and using test equipment such as an oscilloscope for diagnosis
  • Completing planned servicing and preventative maintenance across the full machine
  • Installing and commissioning new machines, including geometric checks, alignments and electrical set-up
  • Working with Fanuc and Okuma controls across both mechanical and electrical work
  • Producing clear service reports and keeping customers updated on findings and work done
 
Skills and Experience
  • A qualification in mechanical or electrical engineering, or a maintenance discipline, with genuine ability across both
  • A good level of experience working on CNC machine tools, including lathes and machining centres
  • Mechanical experience across areas such as ballscrew and linear guide replacement, spindle exchange, gib adjustment and scraping
  • Electrical experience across areas such as fault finding, circuit testing, use of test equipment and drive or power supply replacement
  • Strong fault finding and diagnosis skills across both disciplines
  • Knowledge of wire and sinker EDM machines, which is an advantage
  • Experience with Fanuc and Okuma controls, which is an advantage
  • A full UK driving licence and a willingness to travel across the UK, and occasionally to Europe
Pay and Benefits
  • A basic salary of £40,000 to £42,000, negotiable depending on experience
  • Paid overtime on a door-to-door basis, from the moment you leave home
  • A company car (plug-in hybrid)
  • Laptop, phone, tools and workwear provided
  • Company pension
  • Private healthcare
  • Expenses covered
 
Ready to apply?
A Field Service Engineer who can confidently cover both the mechanical and electrical side are the ones every service operation wants, and they do not come along often. This role rewards that breadth with a company car, full kit, paid door-to-door overtime and the independence to run your own days. If you are a multi-skilled Field Service Engineer who likes seeing a job through from fault to fix, apply now.

job.title: Embedded Software Engineer
job.description:
Embedded Software Engineer
 
Write the embedded C behind smart metering devices shipping over a million units, with a genuine path towards leading the firmware team.
 
This is an Embedded Software Engineer role with an established manufacturer, developing firmware for high-volume metering products.
 
As an Embedded Software Engineer you will design, develop and test the embedded firmware at the heart of an established manufacturer's smart metering products. Working entirely in embedded C on Microchip tools, you will take on new product development, significant redesign work and modular improvements across a product range that ships well over a million units and sees new products every 12 to 18 months. With metering specifications, device language and increasingly cyber security directives all in scope, it is technically meaty work with real ownership. There is also a genuine opportunity here: this role offers a real path towards leading the firmware function in the future as part of a succession plan.
 
Job Responsibilities
  • Designing, developing and testing embedded firmware in embedded C for metering products
  • Carrying out new product development, redesign work and modular improvements across the range
  • Developing firmware to relevant metering specifications and device language standards
  • Building cyber security into firmware in line with new directives and requirements
  • Writing your own test code and building testing into the development process
  • Working within the Microchip toolchain and emulation environment
  • Debugging and validating firmware against hardware
  • Producing clear technical documentation
  • Contributing to design reviews and continuous improvement
 
Skills and Experience
To succeed as an Embedded Software Engineer you will need:
  • Strong, proven experience developing firmware in embedded C
  • A solid maths background
  • Experience taking products through new development and redesign
  • The ability to write test code and build testing into the development process
  • Experience with the Microchip toolchain and emulation environments, which is an advantage
  • An awareness of metering specifications or device language standards, which is desirable
  • An understanding of embedded cyber security requirements, which is desirable
  • Some scripting experience, which is useful
  • A degree in electronics, software or a related discipline, or equivalent experience
 
Pay and Benefits
As an Embedded Software Engineer you will receive:
  • Salary up to £60,000, dependent on experience
  • Monday to Friday working hours
  • International travel opportunities
  • A clear path towards leading the firmware function
  • Varied, hands-on work on high-volume products with regular new development
 
Ready to apply?
Firmware roles that combine genuinely technical embedded C work with a real route into leadership do not come along often. You would own significant development on products that ship in their millions, with the scope to grow into managing the firmware team. If you are an experienced Embedded Software Engineer ready for that step, apply now.

Field Service Engineer - Essex
 
Fed up with 60+ hour weeks, hotel dinners, and missing family time? This Field Service Engineer role offers true work-life balance – and it doesn’t compromise on pay.

Join a global precision machinery manufacturer that values the quality of service over the number of jobs completed.
 
As a CNC Service Engineer, you’ll cover a regional patch within the UK (Essex) – no nationwide scrambling, no constant weeks away from home.  You’ll be the face of the business, servicing, repairing, and installing a high-end range of machinery. There’s no pressure for volume callouts – just quality technical work, backed by optional travel to Europe and training opportunities in Japan. If you’re tired of being overworked and undervalued, this is your chance to change that.
 
Job Responsibilities
  • Install precision machinery including electrical, electronic, and mechanical components to manufacturer specifications
  • Diagnose faults and carry out on-site repair work for CNC and metal-cutting machinery
  • Order replacement parts and complete repairs in line with technical documentation
  • Liaise with the Service Manager on job progress and flag any major customer or technical issues
  • Train customers on general machine maintenance to reduce avoidable callouts
  • Maintain detailed records and documentation for each machine install or service
  • Attend training on new machinery launches to ensure up-to-date product knowledge
  • Work independently and manage your own service schedule
  • Occasionally travel into Europe if desired (optional – not mandatory)
 
Skills and Experience
  • Previous experience as a Field Service Engineer working on high-precision machinery
  • Background in CNC lathes, metal-cutting, or similar equipment essential
  • Strong mechanical and electrical fault-finding skills
  • Confident with PLC systems and ladder logic
  • Able to read and interpret schematics, technical drawings, and manuals
  • Proven ability to manage your own time and workload on the road
 
Pay and Benefits
  • Salary up to £35,000
  • OTE £50,000+ with bonuses
  • Monday to Friday – circa 40 hours per week
  • Company car (BMW 330e or similar)
  • Annual company performance bonus
  • Monthly bonus paid per machine sold
  • Up to 6% matched pension contribution
  • 22 days holiday plus bank holidays
 
This Field Service Engineer role is a genuine opportunity to step away from the burnout of traditional field service work. With structured hours, extensive training & support, and strong bonus potential, it’s a move worth making.

job.title: Electrical Technician
job.description:
Electrical Technician
 
If you would rather be outdoors and hands-on than stuck behind a desk, this is the role for you.
 
This is an Electrical Technician role with a growing renewable energy business near Ely, on a days-only four-on, four-off shift pattern.
 
As an Electrical Technician you will maintain and improve the electrical systems that keep a growing renewable energy operation running safely and efficiently, working on the plants that turn organic waste into clean energy. It is a highly varied, hands-on role, from planned preventative maintenance and fault-finding through to installations, testing, inspections and breakdown response. Be clear on one thing: this is not a desk job. Up to 90% of your time will be spent outdoors across operational plant areas, often at height and in all weathers. If you are a practical, self-motivated Electrical Technician who enjoys problem-solving and wants your skills to count towards a more sustainable future, this role delivers exactly that, on a days-only pattern with real time off.
 
Job Responsibilities
  • Carrying out planned preventative maintenance in line with maintenance schedules
  • Diagnosing and resolving electrical faults across site systems and equipment
  • Performing electrical repairs, installations, inspections and testing to a high standard
  • Modifying and maintaining control panels
  • Supporting breakdown investigations and returning equipment to service quickly and safely
  • Working on motors, drives, instrumentation, control systems and process equipment
  • Fault-finding on three-phase electrical systems and safety circuits
  • Maintaining accurate maintenance records using company logging systems
  • Supporting mechanical maintenance activities where required
  • Working outdoors and at height across operational plant areas, in all weather conditions
 
Skills and Experience
To succeed as an Electrical Technician, you will need:
  • Industrial or manufacturing electrical maintenance experience
  • Experience of electrical breakdown repair, maintenance and installation
  • Strong electrical fault-finding and diagnostics skills
  • Experience of control panel modification, three-phase systems and safety circuits
  • Experience of motor testing, inverter drives and 4-20mA instrumentation and control signals
  • Good mechanical aptitude and confidence working around plant machinery
  • A full UK driving licence and right to work in the UK
 
Desirable
  • PLC and I/O fault-finding, SCADA and industrial networks experience is desirable
  • An HNC, NVQ Level 3 or equivalent, and City & Guilds 2391 or 2392 is desirable
  • A 16th, 17th or 18th Edition wiring regulations qualification, which is desirable
 
Pay and Benefits
As an Electrical Technician you will receive:
  • A salary of up to £40,000 depending on experience
  • A days-only, four-on, four-off, 12-hour shift pattern with overtime available
  • 6am to 6pm
  • 28 days annual leave, including public holidays
  • Workplace pension
  • A company vehicle for travel between sites
  • Full PPE provided
  • Free on-site parking, and free tea and coffee
  • Full training in renewable energy technologies and long-term career development
 
Ready to apply?
If you want a role that combines engineering, problem-solving and outdoor work with genuine long-term prospects, this is one worth looking at. You would help keep critical green-energy infrastructure running, receive specialist training, and build your career in one of the UK's fastest-growing sectors. If you are a practical Electrical Technician ready to get hands-on, apply now.

job.title: Manufacturing Engineer
job.description:
Manufacturing Engineer
 
Strong on welding and fabrication? Be the technical authority behind high-integrity components in one of the most demanding, highly regulated manufacturing environments there is.
 
This is a Manufacturing Engineer role with a respected precision manufacturer.
 
As a Manufacturing Engineer you will be the go-to technical expert for the manufacture of high-integrity components in a highly regulated environment, with welding and fabrication at the very heart of the role. This is a hands-on technical authority role with no direct reports, so your focus stays firmly on the engineering itself, root cause analysis, specifications, and solving the problems that keep complex, regulated manufacturing on track. There is also real scope to help shape the future of the operation, supporting the move towards higher-volume, faster-turnaround manufacturing and developing the processes to make it happen. The business is looking specifically for someone with deep welding and fabrication expertise to lead this area with authority, backed by strong machining and metallurgy knowledge. With a long-term, secured order book behind it, this is a stable, senior role where your expertise genuinely carries the operation.
 
Job Responsibilities
  • Acting as the lead technical authority for welding and fabrication across the manufacture of high-integrity components
  • Providing engineering solutions across welding, fabrication and CNC machining
  • Leading root cause analysis and resolving complex welding, fabrication and manufacturing problems
  • Setting and reviewing welding and fabrication methods to meet the acceptance criteria of a highly regulated industry
  • Supporting the development of higher-volume, reduced-cycle-time manufacturing and the processes to enable it
  • Reviewing and interpreting engineering drawings and specifications, including complex geometries and tight tolerances
  • Supporting new product introduction, design changes and manufacturing strategy
  • Developing and improving engineering processes, procedures and change control
  • Managing non-conformances through robust rework procedures and demonstrating product compliance
  • Raising and controlling technical queries, production permits and concessions
  • Driving cost saving, continuous improvement and defect reduction on the line
  • Acting as a technical point of contact for suppliers, clients and internal teams
 
Skills and Experience
To succeed as a Manufacturing Engineer, you will need:
  • Strong, demonstrable welding and fabrication experience, which is the priority for this role
  • A solid machining and manufacturing background gained in a precision engineering environment
  • Metallurgy experience and a good understanding of high-integrity materials
  • The ability to act as the technical authority on welding and fabrication and lead root cause analysis on complex problems
  • Confidence reading and interpreting engineering drawings and specifications to recognised standards
  • Experience of working within a highly regulated, high-integrity manufacturing environment
  • An interest in developing manufacturing processes to improve volume and reduce cycle times
  • A degree in an engineering or technical discipline
  • Strong communication skills, able to hold technical discussions with clients, suppliers and internal teams
  • A self-motivated, methodical approach, leading through expertise rather than line management
 
Pay and Benefits
As a Manufacturing Engineer you will receive:
  • A salary up to £55,000 depending on experience
  • A company pension with 3% contribution
  • 25 days holiday plus bank holidays
  • A Christmas shutdown of up to 5 days
  • Access to a health and wellbeing platform
  • The stability of a business with a secured, long-term order book
  • A senior, hands-on technical role with real authority and influence
 
Ready to apply?
Roles offering this level of technical authority, in an environment this demanding and this stable, do not come along often. If you are an engineer with genuine welding and fabrication expertise, this is a chance to own that area outright, help drive the operation towards higher-volume, faster manufacturing, and shape how high-integrity work gets done, all with a secured order book behind you. If you are ready to step up as the Manufacturing Engineer, this is one to act on. Apply now.
